I have been farming this 3.8 mu in Quzhou for 30 years, wheat in winter and maize in summer, just like everyone else around here. I finished middle school, so I can read the labels on fertilizer bags and I talk to the seed dealer in town, but most of what I know comes from doing it year after year and watching Old Wang and the others.

For wheat this year, I will rotary till the field before sowing in early October. I plant an improved variety, about 30 jin per mu, which is roughly 15 kg per mu. I buy four bags of compound fertilizer — the kind the dealer says is good for wheat, with more phosphorus in it — and spread that as base fertilizer at sowing. That is a bit more than one 50-jin bag per mu. Then at green-up in spring I topdress with urea, about 20 jin per mu, and again at jointing stage another 25 jin per mu. I would rather put on a little too much nitrogen than risk thin ears; a bad harvest is a disaster, but wasting some fertilizer is just money. I irrigate four times: winter water after the New Year, then at jointing, heading, and grain filling. Diesel for the pump costs me, but dry wheat is worse. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once after sowing, insecticide once when the aphids show up, and fungicide once if the weather turns damp. I expect about 1000 jin per mu, same as last year if the frost does not kill it.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed straight after wheat harvest in early June without plowing — I use the no-till planter. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the row at planting, the high-nitrogen kind for maize. Some people skip topdressing, but I learned that maize gets hungry in July, so I spread another half bag of urea per mu when the plants are knee-high. I irrigate twice: once when the tassels come out and once during grain filling if the summer rain is not enough. I spray herbicide right after planting and insecticide once in August when the worms come. I expect about 1100 jin per mu. My land is small, so every bag of fertilizer and every liter of diesel matters, but I have seen what happens when you cheap out — you get small ears and you regret it all winter.
